steps.content: Falling. Still falling.
A fall with no end.
She's long since grown used to the ground disappearing beneath her feet; things always slide toward disaster the moment she gets involved.
<color=#fb9259>If her bad luck were hers alone to bear, she would have stopped minding a long time ago.</color>
Murphy? Murphy...?
Time to get up. Your alarm's loud enough to wake the whole neighborhood.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Mmm... Okay... Mom...

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: I've got to take your brothers and sisters to school today, so you're on your own. Be careful out there. No accidents this time!

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Mmm... drive safe...
But her misfortune always manages to drag others down with her.
<color=#fb9259>It was like this when she was a child.</color>

steps.speaker: Teacher
steps.content: Hello? Is this Murphy's mother? Murphy was hit by a flower pot during the field trip. It's just a scratch, but we'd really rather you come pick her up.

steps.speaker: Teacher
steps.content: ...Oh, stuck in traffic? All right, we'll take her to the community clinic nearby then.

steps.speaker: Young Murphy
steps.content: I'm sorry... Teacher. I caused trouble for you and Mom.
<color=#fb9259>And it's still like this now that she's grown.</color>
She spent ages preparing for the analyst interview, arrived right on time, only to find someone else's name on the list instead of hers.

steps.speaker: Person-in-Charge
steps.content: Sorry, the analyst applications are closed.

Murphy wanted to protest that registration wasn't even over yet, and that name on the list wasn't even hers. But then the interview room door opened, and she saw the interviewer fawning over someone who never even showed up for the written exam.
The person-in-charge quickly pulled the door shut, fished a random form out of the folder, and shoved it at Murphy.

steps.speaker: Person-in-Charge
steps.content: Look... reception still has an opening. Maybe try your luck there?

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: ...Sorry for the trouble.
When something happens once, people call it a coincidence.
When it happens twice, they call it bad luck.
After three, four, five times, even she started to believe the problem really does lie with her.
Over time, she has learned to apologize first whenever trouble strikes, as if that might soften others' anger, as if owning her misfortune upfront could make it all a little less humiliating.
Another sharp crack tears through the air beside her. She was moments away from leaving this place, and now this.
A red-hot steel beam plunges down from above at an angle, grazing past her shoulder and streaking her vision with blinding sparks.
Murphy instinctively hunches her shoulders, her limbs trying to curl inward just like every other time disaster struck, making herself as small as possible. Maybe this is just how it's meant to be.
But the next moment, she feels a clear, unmistakable grip seize her wrist.
Someone is holding onto her tight, in a freefall where they can barely even save themselves.
Murphy freezes for a second, then opens her eyes to find a blurred figure before her.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: It's... you... ${PlayerName}.
The red light of the shackles stretches between her and ${PlayerName}, pulled taut in their plummet like a thread about to snap.
The howling wind, searing heat, and thunderous roar threaten to swallow her whole. Yet in this instant, one thing becomes absolutely clear.
Even now, ${PlayerName} refuses to let go.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: No...

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: This can't keep happening...
What should have been simple unraveled into disaster. Relaxed faces shifted to weariness and frustration... She was supposed to be blamed again, pushed away again...
But not this time. This time, someone holds on no matter what, without a trace of reproach.
Murphy sets her jaw, her fingers shaking. She wants to meet this trust and the care behind it with something of her own.
With determination verging on clumsy, she squeezes the hand that holds her. She wants to protect her friends, the ones who believe in her without a single condition.
<color=#fb9259>Even if just this once.</color>

You slam into an enormous space far below. The Sinners do what they can to cushion the blow with their abilities, but the truth remains that you've just fallen from the height of a ten-story building.
You force yourself upright. Blood coats the back of your throat, and the raw scrape on your shoulder throbs with sharp, relentless heat.
But what reaches you even faster than the pain is the faint pressure of a hand squeezing back from the other end of your wrist.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: ...Chief...Are you okay?!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm fine. What about the others?

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: Cough, cough... Alive! Barely. Feels like someone took me apart and put me back together all wrong.

steps.speaker: Letta
steps.content: Hmm... nice sound on the landing. Just a little too loud, maybe.

steps.speaker: Lynn
steps.content: I-I'm here..! The coin's safe too!

Everyone lies scattered across the platform, but thankfully, they all manage to respond. Not far off, Lynn kneels at the edge of a fractured ledge, both hands gripping the recovered gold coin in a white-knuckled hold.
You glance back overhead. The opening you fell through has already warped into a hazy smear of red light above, as if something is slowly sealing it shut from the outside.
At the deepest point, ringed by fractured platforms and pools of contaminated sludge, the runes on the alchemy cauldron slowly begin to glow once more.
A pulse follows—agonizingly slow, yet so distinct it crawls across the skin—and the corruption tracing the device's surface flares and dims, swells and shrinks, like breathing.
The cauldron's body rotates toward you, and the mechanical arms fused to it rise with it.

steps.speaker: Alchemy Cauldron
steps.content: Come! Let it all melt away!
